About RR-SGD

RR-SGD: WebGPU-Accelerated Graph Layout with Round-Robin SGD

A 2D graph layout tool that minimizes stress—the discrepancy between graph shortest-path distances and 2D Euclidean distances—using Stochastic Gradient Descent (SGD).

What is Round-Robin (RR)?

Coordinate updates are partitioned into conflict-free Round-Robin matchings so GPU threads never write to the same vertex concurrently, enabling lock-free parallel updates in both Full and Sparse modes.

  • RR Full SGD: Uses all-pairs shortest-path distances. Distance storage scales quadratically with vertex count.
  • RR Sparse SGD: Combines pivot-based constraints and original graph edges using one-sided updates and two-sided matchings to lay out large graphs within bounded memory.

How to Use

  1. Load a built-in sample or choose a Matrix Market (.mtx) file.
  2. Choose Full or Sparse, set iterations and seed, and click “Compute Layout”.
  3. Compare Before and After views, and export layout JSON or PNG as needed.
Implementation & Input Details

Full: All-pairs shortest paths. Tile 128 / workgroup 64 / shared / u16 4-bank.

Sparse: Pivot distances and directional weights. One-sided updates + two-sided matchings / workgroup 128 / shared pivot cache. Per-vertex Feistel permutation shuffles pivot order.

Extracts the largest connected component as an undirected, unweighted graph. Self-loops and duplicate edges are removed; matrix values are ignored.

No fixed 4,096-vertex cap; actual GPU buffer limits are checked before allocation. Select RR Sparse for large graphs.

Files never leave your device. Preprocessing and evaluation run in Web Workers, and SGD runs via Rust + wgpu WebAssembly on the browser WebGPU API.

SGD runs on WebGPU and preprocessing/evaluation run in Web Workers. Selected files are never uploaded to a server. RR Sparse is recommended for large graphs. Maximum graph size depends on GPU memory, and stress is labeled as exact or sampled.
